solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After review, TV cites coffee as good value

indicators.note: a review goes over things again and revises them, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the fodder

explanation.surface: A television programme, having looked into it, recommends coffee as a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After review' reads as a time phrase, but it tells you to rearrange all thirteen letters of TV CITES COFFEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worth the money spent on it is economical, giving good value.

clue.text: Chap, missing home at first, cheers popular team leader

indicators.note: missing means a letter is absent from the word chap
at first points to the opening letter of the word home

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A man who has not been home lately toasts the leader of a well-liked side.
explanation.walkthrough: Chap loses H, the first letter of home, leaving CAP. TA is informal British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is the player who leads a sports side, a synonym for team leader.

clue.text: Source of something to write on Waterloo? I'm not sure

definitions.text: Source of something to write on

parts.note: Waterloo is a major railway station in London
er is the hesitant noise made when unsure

explanation.surface: Someone wonders, hesitantly, whether Waterloo is where you'd find writing paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo is a London railway terminus. The definition is a cryptic way of describing a shop that sells paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer sells paper and envelopes, so is a supplier of material for writing on.

clue.text: Oddly ignored? Well, couple run off

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters are passed over, so only the even letters of the next words are kept

explanation.surface: A strange snub prompts a pair to bolt together.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the 1st, 3rd and so on letters of Well and couple: E L from Well, O P E from couple. 'Couple' looks like part of the definition but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly to marry, so it means to run off.

clue.text: Turned up home provided with outbuilding and needing no more done

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: in means at home
if means provided that
a shed is a small outbuilding

explanation.surface: Someone arrives home to find a garden shed and no chores left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like 'arrived', but in a down clue it means read upwards; it covers both home and provided together.
explanation.definitionFit: A finished job is complete, so nothing further needs doing on it.

clue.text: Work run

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a profession or working life
second meaning: to rush along at speed, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: Two plain words that look like a pair of verbs, but the first sense is a noun for one's working life.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is a lifelong occupation, and to career is to hurtle along uncontrollably.

clue.text: Step in replacing thin veneer, not hard

indicators.note: replacing means putting the letters back in different places, so they are rearranged
not says the letter for hard is left out of the fodder

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A carpenter is told to take over, swapping a flimsy veneer that isn't sturdy.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H (hard, as on pencils) out of THIN VENEER and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To intervene is to get involved in a situation to alter it, which is to step in.

clue.text: Part of hotel I term best

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone describes a stretch of their hotel stay as the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the choicest members of a group, the best of the bunch.

clue.text: One offered to help with the French name

parts.note: a hand is a helping hand, one offered in assistance
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French helper is introduced by name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the pieces. HAND is read as the hand someone holds out to help.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is informal for a person's name or title, as in a nickname.

clue.text: Military unit which is also in scheme

indicators.note: in says one word is placed within the letters of the other

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
too means also

explanation.surface: A military unit is said to be part of some plot as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a subdivision of an army company, a small body of soldiers.

clue.text: Some clarets in Athens or another wine?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A drinker in Greece wonders whether to order claret or a different wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white flavoured with pine resin, a different wine from claret.

clue.text: Arsenal's first team in seclusion

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word Arsenal's

parts.note: a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: The Arsenal first eleven is kept out of the public eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club, which makes 'first team' read as one phrase; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aside means apart or out of the way, removed from others, so privately set apart.

clue.text: Leader of parade, he's out of order

indicators.note: out of order means the letters are not in their proper sequence, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the fodder

explanation.surface: The man at the front of the procession is behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' reads as misbehaving, but it shuffles PARADE HES.
explanation.definitionFit: A spearhead is the person or group at the front of an attack or campaign, its leader.

clue.text: Score just one short

parts.note: a score is twenty, so one short of it is the number before twenty

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a match result missed by a point; 'score' is the old word for twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty less one gives the cardinal number nineteen, a score being twenty.

clue.text: Enduring custom — conduct ultimately helping to protect police officer

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word conduct
to protect means one word surrounds and shields the other

parts.note: a ration is a helping or portion
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A long-standing practice requires guarding officers while they assist.
explanation.walkthrough: A DI is a Detective Inspector in British police ranks; 'helping' is a noun here, a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a practice handed down through generations, a long-lasting custom.

clue.text: Regret hiding key needed for delivery?

indicators.note: hiding means the first word conceals the second inside it

parts.note: to rue is to regret
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry to have concealed the key a courier needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that delivery means saving, not a parcel arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliverance from danger is a rescue, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

clue.text: Rising anger follows review covering standard

indicators.note: follows means the reversed anger comes after the review

parts.note: crit is short for critique, a review

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ire is anger
on means covering, lying upon

explanation.surface: A bad write-up provokes mounting fury that spreads over the norm.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Rising' means read from the bottom up; 'follows' sets the anger after the review.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion is a principle by which something is judged, a standard or yardstick.

clue.text: Pub manager's story about drunken scene

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: a lie is a story, an untruth

indicators.note: drunken means unsteady and reeling, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A landlord tells a tall tale about a boozy incident.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay; in Britain a pub's licensee holds its alcohol licence.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensee holds the licence to sell alcohol, so is the person running a pub.

clue.text: Society the best? A joke!

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of high society being the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hilarious is called a scream, so a very funny person or thing is a joke.

clue.text: Said to be almost used up — about right

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word goes round the other
almost means the word falls one letter short, dropping its end

parts.note: spent means used up, exhausted
OK means all right, correct

explanation.surface: Someone is reported to be nearly exhausted, more or less correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims the final letter from the word for used up; 'to be' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken means uttered aloud in words, the past participle of speak, just as said is.

clue.text: Linger around after greeting mercenary

indicators.note: after means the rearranged word follows the greeting

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved about, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A hired soldier lingers about after saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like it means hanging about, but it signals that the letters of Linger are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A hireling works only for pay, and a mercenary is a hired soldier motivated by money.

clue.text: Rock music style with second-class content? Nonsense

indicators.note: content means the second-class letter is held within, as contents

parts.note: garage is a style of raw rock music
B is the grade below A, second class

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a mediocre rock genre as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as satisfied but means contents: B goes inside GARAGE. 'With' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is rubbish, and figuratively worthless talk or ideas, nonsense.

clue.text: Instructed with Charlie for time? Heard accurately

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: taught means instructed
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A pupil was taught with someone called Charlie but asks if they heard properly.
explanation.walkthrough: In TAUGHT, the T for time is swapped for C. 'Heard accurately' sounds like a homophone signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: If you caught what someone said, you made it out clearly, as in 'I didn't catch that'.

clue.text: Self-willed former pupil's essentially fine in gallery

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: in means the middle letters sit within the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: essentially points to the core letters of the word fine, its middle

explanation.surface: An old boy's stubborn streak shows, though his core is fine, at the gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British art galleries in London and elsewhere; an old boy is a former pupil of a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obstinate stubbornly refuses to change course, which is being self-willed.

clue.text: Authoritarian back

definitions.meaning: first meaning: strict and severe, as an adjective
second meaning: the rear part of a ship

explanation.walkthrough: Back looks like a verb or adjective, but the sense needed is nautical: the rear of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern describes a harsh disciplinarian, and the stern is the after part of a vessel.

clue.text: Barb from son? Never! Heartless!

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: never is the full word before its centre is removed

explanation.surface: A cruel remark from a son? That's unthinkable, and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' reads as cruel, but it removes the central letter of the word Never.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneer is a scornful remark, and a barb is a cutting comment.

clue.text: Street with exhibition area

parts.note: and means with, together with

explanation.surface: A road beside a showground.
explanation.definitionFit: At a trade fair each exhibitor has a stand, the booth or space where goods are displayed.

clue.text: Period of levelling off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the time of day between afternoon and night
second meaning: making smooth or flat, the -ing form of even

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a plateau; 'of' links two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening is the late part of the day, and evening something is making it flat.

clue.text: Enduring quality of good person in morning I note, admirable from outset

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good person
a.m. means in the morning
n. is the abbreviation for note, as in footnotes

indicators.note: from outset points to the opening letter of the word admirable

explanation.surface: A saintly person's morning endurance is praised as admirable from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: N for note comes from footnote references (n.), not from music.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the staying power to keep going for a long time, an enduring quality.

clue.text: Absence of new tenant, back working earlier, observed at social event

indicators.note: earlier means that reversed piece comes first
back means the word for working is read backwards

parts.note: on means working, functioning

indicators.note: new means the letters of tenant are made afresh, rearranged

parts.note: a dance is a social event

explanation.surface: A new tenant, having returned to work early, was seen at a party, so missed something.
explanation.walkthrough: ON reversed is NO; TENANT rearranged gives NATTEN; then DANCE. 'Observed at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-attendance means failing to turn up, which is an absence from somewhere.
